props.title: The Adventures of Robin Hood
props.initialSlug: Outlaw hero, rebel with a cause.

sections.content: The Adventures of Robin Hood (1938) revolutionized action-adventure filmmaking through its masterful blend of swashbuckling excitement and Technicolor splendor. Errol Flynn's definitive portrayal of Robin Hood set the template for every heroic archer since, while Michael Curtiz and William Keighley's dynamic direction established conventions still used in modern adventure films. The film's influence echoes through later medieval epics like Ivanhoe (1952) and The Court Jester (1956), while its "rob from the rich, give to the poor" ethos inspired social justice themes in everything from Zorro (1940) to Batman Begins (2005).

sections.content: The film's technical achievements were groundbreaking for 1938. The three-strip Technicolor process captured the verdant Sherwood Forest and rich medieval costumes with unprecedented vibrancy. The archery sequences, performed by expert Howard Hill in long shots, set new standards for action choreography. These innovations influenced later technicolor adventures like The Black Swan (1942) and The Masters of Ballantrae (1953), proving that technical excellence and pure entertainment could coexist.

Olivia de Havilland's Marian and Basil Rathbone's Sir Guy of Gisbourne established character archetypes that persist in adventure cinema. Their performances elevated the material beyond simple heroics, creating a template for the strong-willed heroine and sophisticated villain that would influence films from The Princess Bride (1987) to Pirates of the Caribbean (2003). The chemistry between Flynn and de Havilland, in their third of eight collaborations, defined romantic adventure for a generation. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Modern Influence

sections.content: The film's influence extends far beyond period adventures. Its basic story structure - an aristocrat fighting corruption from outside the system - appears in countless modern films like V for Vendetta (2005) and The Dark Knight (2008). The iconic archery tournament scene has been referenced or recreated in everything from Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves (1991) to Disney's animated Robin Hood (1973), while the film's blend of humor and action influenced modern adventures like The Mask of Zorro (1998).
